source.title: The Effect of Label Noise on the Information Content of Neural Representations
source.authors: Ali Hussaini Umar; Franky Kevin Nando Tezoh; Jean Barbier; Santiago Acevedo; Alessandro Laio

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendix are present. Figure graphics are not available as extractable numerical data.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps network width and measures generalization error, directly testing model-size double descent with the same general intervention and outcome as the original claim, in different network and dataset settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test-error and information-imbalance width sweeps in Figure 2. Individual plotted values and exact label-noise levels are not stated in the text, so those rows retain figure-only values. Epoch-wise and sample-size double descent are discussed through citations, not tested here. Other representation comparisons and cross-entropy analyses do not measure test error and are not included as V1/V6 rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 2(a),(d) report the study's own width sweeps of generalization error under several label-noise levels. The FCNN/MNIST setup follows Belkin et al. (4,000 training samples). This directly tests model-wise double descent (V1) and its label-noise dependence (V6). The study's main focus is representation similarity, which bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is partly wrong. The authors conclude that hidden-representation Information Imbalance mirrors the test-error double descent across width. They find that overparameterized hidden representations are largely unaffected by label noise, being equally informative with or without moderate noise. Information loss between the penultimate and pre-softmax layers grows with label noise and tracks cross-entropy loss, which they propose as an unsupervised generalization tool. Representations trained on random labels are less informative than random features. The authors do not say that the representation results are distinct from test error. They note one difference: II decays to zero in the overparameterized regime while error does not.
record.recipe_differences: Uses width sweeps and generalization error as in model-size double-descent studies, but tests a single-layer FCNN on MNIST and a CNN on CIFAR-10, with label-noise conditions, and additionally studies representation information.
record.method_sensitivity: The generalization-error peak height increases with label-noise level. In the MNIST FCNN, the clean-label peak is described as very small; in the underparameterized CIFAR-10 CNN, label noise does not significantly affect error.

fits_no_version.finding: Information Imbalance between the hidden representations of independently initialized networks follows a width-wise double-descent shape. Its first minimum is near the test-error minimum. It decays to zero in the overparameterized regime at every noise level, whereas test error does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mutual predictivity of independently trained networks' hidden representations shows width-wise double descent that tracks test error up to the overparameterized regime.

fits_no_version.finding: In the underparameterized regime, label noise lowers test error for MNIST and does not significantly change it for CIFAR-10 (Section 3.2). No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Below the interpolation threshold, moderate label noise can act as a regularizer rather than raising test error.

record.problems: The empirical test-error evidence covers only a single-layer FCNN on MNIST and a CNN on CIFAR-10. Test-error values are presented in figures without extractable numerical values in the supplied text, exact label-noise levels are not stated in the text, and no epoch-wise or near-threshold sample-size test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other direct test-error results on the claim were reported. Epoch-wise and sample-size double-descent findings in Appendix A.1 are attributed to prior work and were excluded. Figures 3–5 report representation comparisons or classifier results on representations, not the test-error curves required for these claim versions.

untested.parts: Only a single-layer FCNN on MNIST and a 4-stage CNN on CIFAR-10 were tested. No other architectures or datasets were tested, and no interpolation-threshold location is reported numerically.
Variance as a driver, triple or multiple descent, and removal of the peak by optimally tuned regularization were not tested.
Not tested; it is only cited from Nakkiran et al.
Not tested. Figure 5 scales N and P together at a fixed ratio and measures representation II and probe accuracy.
Not tested; only neural networks were used.

record.verdict_notes: All test-error evidence is figure-only (Fig. 2a,d), and exact label-noise levels are not stated in the text. The MNIST setup replicates the Belkin et al. (original source) protocol, but this study is not itself an original source, so verdicts apply. Pre-softmax II (Fig. 2c,f), Figs. 3-5 and the Gaussian bound analyses do not measure test error against width, so they bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests the model-size curve only for a single-layer FCNN on MNIST and a CNN on CIFAR-10; it does not test other architectures or datasets.
No test-error sweep over training epochs is reported.
The study does not vary sample size near the interpolation threshold while measuring test error. Figure 5 scales sample size and parameters proportionally at a fixed ratio and reports other outcomes.
The study tests two neural-network architectures, not double descent across model classes generally.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample size.

The study tests how label-noise levels relate to the model-size test-error peak. It does not test variance as a driver, multiple or triple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not re-express the curve using an effective parameter count or test whether that makes the second descent an ordinary U-shaped curve.
